title: Boss: the zone outage postmortem
summary: Turn a real postmortem timeline into numbers: time to detect, mitigate and resolve, the error budget it burned, and the review findings that become action items.

steps.title: The postmortem draft on your desk
body: Checkout had a bad afternoon. The incident commander wrote this draft and asked you, as the reviewer, to
fill in the numbers and the findings before Friday's review. Tags in capitals mark the key moments.
Postmortem: checkout errors during a zone outage (2026-10-14)
SLO: 99.9% of checkout requests succeed, 30-day window
Architecture: 3 zones, 30 app instances at 72% CPU at peak; PostgreSQL primary in zone b,
asynchronous replica in zone c, no automatic failover
13:52 START     Packet loss begins in zone b
13:58 DETECT    Burn-rate page fires (14.4x over 1 h and 5 min)
14:06           On-call joins; errors come from zone b app servers
14:19 MITIGATE  Zone b drained from the load balancer by hand; errors back under the SLO
14:31           Writes still slow: the primary is in zone b
15:05 RESOLVE   Zone b recovers; traffic rebalanced
Each step below is one piece of the review. They build on each other: the starter of each step contains

steps.title: Minutes between two times
prompt: Write `int MinutesBetween(string from, string to)` for times written `HH:mm`. If `to` is earlier than `from`, the
incident crossed midnight: add a day (1,440 minutes).
`MinutesBetween("13:52", "13:58")` is `6`; `MinutesBetween("23:50", "00:10")` is `20`.
hints: Hours are `t[..2]` and minutes `t[3..5]`; turn both times into minutes since midnight.
A negative difference means the next day: add 1,440.

steps.title: Detect, mitigate, resolve
prompt: Write `(int Detect, int Mitigate, int Resolve) Metrics(string[] timeline)`. Each line starts with `HH:mm`;
after it, the first word may be a tag: `START`, `DETECT`, `MITIGATE` or `RESOLVE`. Lines without a tag are
notes. Return the minutes from `START` to each of the other three. If any of the four tags is missing, throw
`InvalidOperationException` (a postmortem without them is not finished).
For the draft's timeline the answer is `(6, 27, 73)`. Your `MinutesBetween` is in the starter.
starter: (int Detect, int Mitigate, int Resolve) Metrics(string[] timeline)
solution: (int Detect, int Mitigate, int Resolve) Metrics(string[] timeline)
if (tag is "START" or "DETECT" or "MITIGATE" or "RESOLVE") at[tag] = line[..5];
if (!at.ContainsKey(need)) throw new InvalidOperationException($"the timeline has no {need} line");
hints: The time is `line[..5]`; the tag is the first word of `line[5..].Trim()`.
Collect tag -> time in a dictionary, check all four are there, then call `MinutesBetween` three times.
template: "13:52 START     Packet loss begins in zone b",
"13:58 DETECT    Burn-rate page fires (14.4x over 1 h and 5 min)",
"14:06           On-call joins; errors come from zone b app servers",
"14:19 MITIGATE  Zone b drained from the load balancer by hand",
"14:31           Writes still slow: the primary is in zone b",
"15:05 RESOLVE   Zone b recovers; traffic rebalanced" };
var dojoNight = Metrics(new[] { "23:55 START a", "23:59 DETECT b", "00:20 MITIGATE c", "01:00 RESOLVE d" });

Dojo.Eq("notes that mention a tag word later do not count", 6, Metrics(new[] { "10:00 START x", "10:02 On-call asks when DETECT fired", "10:06 DETECT page", "10:10 MITIGATE y", "10:20 RESOLVE z" }).Detect);
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("no RESOLVE line", () => Metrics(new[] { "10:00 START x", "10:05 DETECT y", "10:09 MITIGATE z" }));

steps.title: How much error budget did it burn?
prompt: Write `double BudgetSpentPercent(double[] errorRatePerMinute, double slo, int windowDays)`: the share of the
window's error budget the incident used, in percent. Each array entry is the fraction of requests that failed
in one minute (assume steady traffic, so a minute at 31% errors costs 0.31 "bad minutes"). The budget is
`windowDays x 1,440 x (1 - slo)` minutes. A rate below 0 or above 1 throws `ArgumentException`.
The draft's 38 minutes (6 at 5%, 21 at 31%, 11 at 2%) against 99.9% over 30 days is about `16.3`%.
starter: double BudgetSpentPercent(double[] errorRatePerMinute, double slo, int windowDays)
solution: double BudgetSpentPercent(double[] errorRatePerMinute, double slo, int windowDays)
if (errorRatePerMinute.Any(r => r < 0 || r > 1)) throw new ArgumentException("error rates are fractions from 0 to 1");
hints: Bad minutes are the sum of the per-minute error rates.
Budget minutes: `windowDays * 1440 * (1 - slo)`; the answer is bad / budget x 100.
template: Dojo.Eq("the draft's incident against 99.9% / 30 days", 16.3, Math.Round(BudgetSpentPercent(dojoRates, 0.999, 30), 1));
Dojo.Eq("10 minutes fully down blows a 99.99% budget", 231.5, Math.Round(BudgetSpentPercent(Enumerable.Repeat(1.0, 10).ToArray(), 0.9999, 30), 1));
Dojo.Eq("a clean hour costs nothing", 0.0, BudgetSpentPercent(new double[60], 0.999, 30));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("an error rate of 120% is an error", () => BudgetSpentPercent(new[] { 0.1, 1.2 }, 0.999, 30));

steps.title: The review findings
prompt: Write `List<string> Findings(int detectMinutes, int mitigateMinutes, bool mitigatedByHand, double utilAfterZoneLoss, bool primaryStuckInFailedZone)`
that turns the numbers into findings for the review, in this order:
1. `detectMinutes > 5`: `"detect: the page took {detectMinutes} min; target 5"`
2. `mitigateMinutes > 15` **and** `mitigatedByHand`: `"mitigate: {mitigateMinutes} min by hand; automate the zone drain"`
3. `utilAfterZoneLoss > 0.8`: `"capacity: {percent}% after losing a zone; target 80%"` where `percent` is
`Math.Round(utilAfterZoneLoss * 100)`
4. `primaryStuckInFailedZone`: `"database: the primary stayed in the failed zone; enable automatic failover"`
The draft: 72% CPU over 3 zones is 108% after losing one. `Findings(6, 27, true, 1.08, true)` returns all four.
starter: List<string> Findings(int detectMinutes, int mitigateMinutes, bool mitigatedByHand, double utilAfterZoneLoss, bool primaryStuckInFailedZone)
solution: List<string> Findings(int detectMinutes, int mitigateMinutes, bool mitigatedByHand, double utilAfterZoneLoss, bool primaryStuckInFailedZone)
if (detectMinutes > 5) found.Add($"detect: the page took {detectMinutes} min; target 5");
if (mitigateMinutes > 15 && mitigatedByHand) found.Add($"mitigate: {mitigateMinutes} min by hand; automate the zone drain");
if (utilAfterZoneLoss > 0.8) found.Add($"capacity: {Math.Round(utilAfterZoneLoss * 100)}% after losing a zone; target 80%");
if (primaryStuckInFailedZone) found.Add("database: the primary stayed in the failed zone; enable automatic failover");
hints: Four independent `if`s in the order given, each adding one interpolated string.
`Math.Round(1.08 * 100)` is `108`; interpolating a whole double prints no decimals.
template: Dojo.Eq("the draft: every finding", new List<string> {
"mitigate: 27 min by hand; automate the zone drain",
"database: the primary stayed in the failed zone; enable automatic failover" },
Dojo.Eq("a well-run incident: nothing to say", new List<string>(), Findings(4, 9, false, 0.7, false));
Dojo.Eq("exactly on target is fine", new List<string>(), Findings(5, 15, true, 0.8, false));
Dojo.Eq("automated but slow mitigation is not this finding", new List<string> { "detect: the page took 12 min; target 5" },
Dojo.Eq("capacity only", new List<string> { "capacity: 93% after losing a zone; target 80%" }, Findings(3, 10, true, 0.93, false));
